title: 10. Exercises: Day 18 — Tool Ecosystems
summary: Define @tool def categorize_email(email_id: str) -> str: that returns a category string based on heuristics (sender domain, subject keywords).
objectives: Solve the Day 18 — Tool Ecosystems exercises without looking at the lesson
Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: Exercises
sections.body:
1. **Add a `categorize_email` tool.** Before deciding an action, the agent calls `categorize_email(email_id)` which returns one of `action_required`, `social`, `notification`, `newsletter`. Update the system prompt to use the category to pick the action.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

Define `@tool def categorize_email(email_id: str) -> str:` that returns a category string based on heuristics (sender domain, subject keywords). Update the system prompt: "First call list_inbox, then categorize_email for each, then take the action matching the category: action_required -> reply or create_task; social -> reply; notification -> mark_read or forward; newsletter -> archive."
</details>

2. **Add a per-tool cost ceiling to the nested summarizer.** If `summarize_doc` is called more than 5 times in one outer-agent run, return an error string instead of calling the nested LLM.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

Use a module-level counter `_NESTED_CALLS = 0`. In `summarize_doc`, increment and check: `global _NESTED_CALLS; _NESTED_CALLS += 1; if _NESTED_CALLS > 5: return DocSummary(name=name, summary="RATE_LIMITED", key_points=[])`. Reset the counter at the start of each outer run. For a cleaner approach, use a class instance holding the counter and pass via Pydantic AI deps.
</details>

3. **Replace mock docs with real files.** Point `DOCS` at a directory of `.md` files. Add a `read_doc_chunk(name, offset, length)` tool so the agent can paginate through long documents.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

`import pathlib; DOCS_DIR = pathlib.Path("./docs")`. Rewrite `list_docs` to return sorted filenames. Rewrite `read_doc` to `return (DOCS_DIR / name).read_text()`. Add `read_doc_chunk(name: str, offset: int, length: int) -> str` that returns `text[offset:offset+length]` plus a `has_more: bool` flag. Update the system prompt to encourage chunked reading for docs over 4000 chars.
</details>
